chapter: Bennie Moten, Basie and the Reno
title: The disastrous second New York trip
summary: Goodwin says Moten tried to play the Eastern style the audience had not hired them for, and the trip failed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Didn't they go back to New York again?
They took a disastrous trip to New York the second time.
Well, what happened the second time?
Well, first of all, they tried to change their style of playing. They tried to play what the Easterners were playing.
This was Meter in New York the second time?

That's right. This was the wrong thing to do because they wasn't hired to play that kind of music. They was hired because of the music they played and the music that the people had heard as a Meter aggregation on records, see. Benny recorded for Victor Records at the time. He had done quite a bit of recording for Victor Records.
This would be like in the late '20s I suppose?
Yes.
Do you remember any places they played in New York?
Not really except the Apollo Theatre.
Did they play mostly up in Harlem or did they play downtown too, do you know?
Well, they did some broadcasting in New York and it's just too vague for me to remember where they did play.
But you do remember it was a disastrous trip?
It was a disastrous trip because the second time they had to do more -- play shows, you know, and Basie was a good man for playing these shows because he was
from the East and he understood what went on in the East.
What had to be done, but anyway, the trip was a disaster. They ran out of bookings I suppose --
Right.
-- the reviews weren't good?
They changed their style --
And they came back to Kansas City and go back on one nighters or what happened then?
